description: DA3408 A4: CPU BLIP image captioning app (Streamlit) monitored with Prometheus, node_exporter and Grafana.

panels.description: Guide to the layout of the dashboard.

options.content:
**CPU image captioning app (BLIP base) — Streamlit + prometheus_client + node_exporter.** Read top → bottom: **① Health** (is it up?) → **② Throughput & latency** (how fast?) → **③ Workload & model** (what is it processing?) → **④ Clients** (who is using it?) → **⑤ System resources** (what does it cost the machine?).

🟧 **Orange shaded bands** on every graph = a **bulk ZIP job was running** — use them to match app spikes with CPU/RAM. Colours use the colour-blind safe Okabe-Ito palette; series also differ by **line style** (solid / dashed / dotted) so graphs work in print & grayscale. Hover the ⓘ icon on any panel for its story. Use the **mode** filter (top) to isolate single vs bulk traffic.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard
① Service health — is everything up?

panels.description: Prometheus `up` metric for every scrape target. UP = Prometheus reached the /metrics endpoint in the last scrape, DOWN = it did not (app crashed / exporter stopped).
panels.title: Target health — scrape status per job

panels.description: 1 when the BLIP model has finished loading into memory, 0 while loading. Captions are only possible when LOADED.
panels.title: Model status — BLIP loaded in RAM

panels.description: Time since the Streamlit process started (from the default process collector). A reset to ~0 means the app restarted.
panels.title: App uptime — since process start

panels.description: Requests being processed right now (Gauge) and images waiting for the single-model CPU lock. Non-zero waiting means users are queueing.
panels.title: In progress — requests & queued images

panels.description: Number of Prometheus alert rules currently firing (app down, high latency, high CPU, low memory...). Details at Prometheus /alerts and Alertmanager :9093.
panels.title: Firing alerts — Prometheus rules

panels.description: Counter of successfully captioned images, split by Single vs Bulk mode.
panels.title: Images captioned — total since start

panels.description: Share of images that failed (corrupt / too large / inference error) over the last 5 minutes. 0% is healthy, the alert fires above 20%.
panels.title: Error ratio — failed images (last 5 min)

panels.description: End-to-end latency per request computed from the Summary: rate(_sum)/rate(_count) over 5 minutes. Single = one image, Bulk = one whole ZIP job.
panels.title: Average request latency — Summary (_sum / _count)

panels.description: Browser sessions opened (custom session_id label) and ZIP files uploaded for bulk processing.
panels.title: Sessions & ZIP uploads — total
② Throughput & latency — how fast is the app?

panels.description: Successful images per second by mode (rate of the Counter over 1 min). Bulk jobs show a sustained plateau; single uploads show short blips. Errors per second are shown for comparison.
panels.title: Throughput — images captioned per second

panels.description: Percentiles of model generate() time per image from the Histogram buckets (1 min window). p99 far above p50 means some images are much slower (big images, CPU contention during bulk). Log scale so small and large values are both visible.
panels.title: Inference latency — p50 / p95 / p99 per image (Histogram)

panels.description: Average end-to-end latency from the Summary metric (rate of _sum / rate of _count). A bulk request covers a whole ZIP so it is much longer than a single request — hence the log scale.

custom.axisLabel: Avg latency per request (seconds, log₂ scale)

panels.title: Request latency — single image vs whole ZIP job (Summary)

panels.description: Average time per image spent decoding/resizing the image (preprocess) vs running the model (inference). Inference dominates on CPU, so that is where optimisation matters.

custom.axisLabel: Avg time per image (seconds, log₂ scale)

panels.title: Where time goes — preprocessing vs model inference

panels.description: Each column is a time slice, each row a latency bucket (seconds); brighter = more images landed in that bucket. Shows the whole spread of latencies, not just percentiles. Viridis colour scale is colour-blind safe.
panels.title: Latency distribution — inference time heatmap
③ Workload & model — what is being processed?

panels.description: Gauge counting down the images still waiting in the current ZIP job, plus active requests by mode. A staircase down to 0 = a healthy bulk job.
panels.title: Bulk progress — images left in the running ZIP job

panels.description: Failed images by error type (bad_image, too_large, inference...) and files skipped inside ZIPs (not an image, hidden __MACOSX files, over the 100 image limit). Shows the app degrading gracefully instead of crashing.
panels.title: Errors & skipped ZIP entries — per minute, by reason

panels.description: Cumulative Histogram buckets: each bar = number of captions with at most N words (since start). The jump between two bars shows where most captions fall. More beams usually gives slightly longer captions.
panels.title: Caption length — distribution of words per caption (Histogram)

panels.description: Average uploaded image size (Histogram _sum/_count, left axis) and resolution in megapixels (Summary, right axis). Bigger images cost more preprocessing time.
panels.title: Input size — average bytes & megapixels per image

panels.description: p95 time to finish a whole ZIP (Histogram, left axis) next to the average number of images per ZIP (Summary, right axis). Duration should grow roughly linearly with ZIP size on a CPU.
panels.title: ZIP jobs — job duration p95 & images per ZIP

panels.description: Static facts about the model: parameter count, how long it took to load, and the current resident memory (RSS) of the app process (psutil Gauge).
panels.title: Model footprint — size, load time, RAM
④ Clients — who is using the app? (custom labels)

panels.description: Requests (single uploads + ZIP jobs) grouped by the client_ip label captured from the Streamlit request context.
panels.title: Requests per client IP — total

panels.description: Most active browser sessions (session_id label, one per browser tab) with their IP. Useful to spot a single user flooding the CPU with ZIPs.
panels.title: Top 10 sessions — requests per session_id

panels.description: Requests per minute split by the browser label (parsed from User-Agent) and mode. Shows which clients generate load over time.
panels.title: Request rate by browser & mode
⑤ System resources — does the hardware follow the app? (node_exporter)

panels.description: Machine CPU % (node_exporter) and the app process CPU % (share of all cores) on the left axis, captioned images/second on the right axis. During bulk jobs (orange bands) CPU and throughput rise together — proving the CPU load comes from the model.

custom.axisLabel: CPU utilisation (% of all cores, linear)

panels.title: CPU vs throughput — correlation of machine CPU with captioning

panels.description: Used RAM of the machine (MemTotal - MemAvailable) next to the resident memory of the Streamlit process. The ~1 GB step at startup is the BLIP model loading; bulk jobs add temporary image buffers.
panels.title: Memory — machine RAM used vs app process RAM

panels.description: How the machine CPU time is split. Model inference shows up as 'user' time; high 'iowait' would mean the disk is the bottleneck instead.

custom.axisLabel: CPU time (% of all cores, linear)

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node", mode=~"user|system|iowait"}[1m])) / scalar(count(count by (cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node", mode="idle"})))

panels.title: CPU breakdown — user / system / iowait

panels.description: 1 and 5 minute load average against the number of cores. Load above the core count means work is queueing for the CPU.
panels.title: Load average vs CPU cores

panels.description: Bytes per second read from and written to physical disks. Spikes at startup = model weights read from the HuggingFace cache; otherwise captioning is CPU-bound, not disk-bound.
panels.title: Disk I/O — read & write throughput

panels.description: Percentage of the root (/) filesystem in use. Turns orange above 80% and vermillion above 90% (DiskAlmostFull alert).

targets.expr: 100 * (1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="node", mountpoint="/", fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="node", mountpoint="/", fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay"})

panels.title: Disk usage — root filesystem

panels.description: Bytes per second in and out of the network interfaces. Uploading a big ZIP through the browser shows as a receive spike right before the bulk band starts.
panels.title: Network — receive & transmit throughput

panels.description: Hardware the app runs on (node_exporter) and the current machine CPU usage, for context when reading the graphs above.
panels.title: Machine facts — cores, RAM, CPU now

title: Image Captioning — Application & System Observability
